correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the exact objective (|<u,x>|^4+|<v,x>|^4)/2. Projection to span{u,v} strictly improves objective for a nonzero perpendicular component. For 0<c<1, relative-phase alignment optimizes the second overlap and reduces the unit-vector problem to G(theta)=[cos^4(theta)+cos^4(theta-phi)]/2 on 0<=theta<=phi=arccos c. With y=cos(2theta-phi) ranging through [c,1], G=(2-c^2+2cy+(2c^2-1)y^2)/4. When 0<c<1/2, its strict concave vertex y*=c/(1-2c^2) is in (c,1) with exactly two angle/ray preimages. When 1/2<=c<1, derivative of this quadratic on [c,1] is positive except possibly at the endpoint c=1/2,y=1, giving only the bisector ray. Endpoints c=0 (two orthogonal generator rays) and c=1 (the common ray) are handled separately. Substitution yields R^2=(1-c^2)^2/[2(1-2c^2)] below c=1/2 and (1+c)^2/4 above. The exact squared branch difference is (1+c)^2(1-2c)^2/[4(1-2c^2)], leading to 1-y*=6delta+O(delta^2), angular splitting 2sqrt(3delta)+O(delta^(3/2)) and radius excess 3delta^2+O(delta^3). Independent SymPy expansion confirmed all polynomial identities, boundary values and second derivatives 19/2 vs 1/2. Finite rational sample checks are only corroboration; the polynomial and phase argument prove the full stated range and dimensional generality.

value.rationale: An exact extremizer transition for the smallest noncommuting projection pair is a natural and potentially valuable invariant in isolation. But the assessed p=2 claim, both branches, and 1-vs-2 maximizing rays are already part of the DISTINCT published, strictly broader p-joint theorem for all real p>=1. Its additional printed square-root angular splitting and quadratic gain are straightforward Taylor expansions of the same prior exact quadratic optimizer and branch difference; they do not constitute an independent new classification, structural lemma, counterexample, or unknown invariant. The correct result therefore lacks distinct scientific contribution relative to strong published coverage, rather than being dismissed for being finite/simple. Its singular coefficients might be useful exposition but do not change the decision.
